name: MA-04
label: Safe D

key_factors: Incumbent Jake Auchincloss running with large financial advantage ($7.3M cash vs $1.3K)
Prediction markets price Democratic win at ~97%
model.rationale: The baseline's Safe D rating is fully supported: a D+11 seat, a well-funded incumbent, and a Republican challenger with negligible fundraising. No evidence justifies moving away from the fundamentals-based forecast.
model.watch: A late surge of outside spending against Auchincloss or an unexpected scandal could narrow the margin, though a Republican win remains highly unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Massachusetts' 4th District leans solidly Democratic, with a partisan advantage of about 11 points. Incumbent Jake Auchincloss is running for reelection after easily securing his party's nomination. He enters the general election with a commanding financial position, having raised over $3.6 million and holding more than $7.3 million in cash.

Republican challenger Thomas Stalcup has raised only about $26,000 and has minimal cash on hand, giving him little capacity to compete. There are no public general-election polls or expert ratings for this race, but prediction markets put the Democratic win probability near 97%. The fundamentals-based model projects a Democratic margin of roughly 22 points, consistent with a Safe D rating.
